item.title: Aged Eggnog
item.description:
https://altonbrown.com/recipes/aged-eggnog/

Phase 1

Ingredients

  • 12 large eggs
  • 1 cup Jamaican rum (Appleton Estates 8, 43% ABV)
  • 1 cup cognac (Ferrand 1840, 45% ABV)
  • 1 cup bourbon (Old Forrester, 50% ABV)
  • 1 cup whole milk
  • 1 pound sugar
  • 2/3 teaspoon numeg, grated

Directions

  1. Separate the egg yolks from the egg whites and place the yolks in a 2-quart container. Freeze the whites into cube for another application.
  2. Combine the rum, cognac, and bourbon in a separate vessel with a pour spout and set aside.
  3. Add the milk to the egg yolks along with the sugar and nutmeg and blend with a stick blender until smooth. Try to keep the head of the blender well-submerged so that you whip up as little foam as possible.
  4. With the motor of the blender still running, slowly pour the spirits into the yolk mixture and blend until fully incorporated.
  5. Place the lid on the container and refrigerate for 30 days. (I typically transfer the mix to 2-quart jars with tight lids as they’re easier to stash long term in the fridge.)
  6. During the first phase aging, remember to shake the jars from time to time.

Phase 2

Ingredients

  • 1 cup whole milk
  • 1 pint half-and-half
  • 1 pint heavy cream
  • 1/3 teaspoon nutmeg, grated

Directions

  1. Remove the phase 1 mixture from the fridge, (If you went with the 2-jar option, recombine into a single vessel that will hold at least 3 quarts.) Place the stick blender into the mixture and blend on medium speed. With the motor running, slowly add the milk, half and half, heavy cream, and nutmeg and blend until smooth. (The order doesn’t matter. You could also combine them all and add at once.)
  2. Return the lid to the container and refrigerate for 50-60 days. (You can divide the eggnog into a few smaller containers as long as they seal tightly.) Again, occasional shaking will help keep things nice and homogenized.
  3. Serve straight from the fridge and remember, it’s tasty but strong. As for long term storage, I can only say that I’ve kept unopened jars for 6 months without any reduction in quality. I have friends who swear by a year but mine almost never last that long because the stuff’s tasty, you know?

item.title: Zucchini Fritteresque
item.description:
https://altonbrown.com/recipes/zucchini-fritteresque/

Ingredients

  • 1 medium zucchini (10 oz)
  • 3 scallions, sliced
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons dried dill
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon + 1 teaspoon all-purpose flour
  • 1 tablespoon + 1 teaspoon white rice flour
  • 1 tablespoon + 1 teaspoon potato starch
  • 2 large eggs, beaten
  • 6 tablespoons Parmesano Reggiano, grated
  • 1/4 cup light olive oil

Directions

  1. Shred the zucchini on the large holes of a box grater onto a piece of parchment paper and dump into a colander set over a bowl or the sink. Add in the scallions, dill, salt, and pepper, and combine well. Drain for 15 minutes, stirring by hand every few minutes.
  2. Combine the all-purpose flour, rice flour, and potato starch in a small bowl and set aside.
  3. Press the zucchini against the side of the colander to squeeze out more moisture then move to a clean kitchen towel and twist into a wad to extract as much liquid as possible.
  4. Empty the zucchini wad onto a half sheet pan and separate the clumps as best as you can. Sprinkle the flour mixture over the zucchini tossing and separating the shreds until no clumps remain. Spread into an even layer and let it dry for 10 minutes.
  5. Pour the olive oil into a 12-inch cast iron skillet over medium heat and let it get hot for 2 minutes. Scatter the zucchini over the surface of the oil, covering the entire bottom of the pan. It should look kind of like lace. Do not press down, just let it begin to brown.
  6. After about 3 minutes, start gently pressing down with a flexible spatula to get more of the zucchini to make contact with the oil, but don’t make it a flat sheet. It should remain craggy in spots.
  7. Meanwhile, add the parmesan cheese to the eggs and set aside.
  8. After about 5 minutes of cooking, lift the edge of the zucchini and check the level of browning. It should be almost mahogany in color. If not, continue cooking until it gets there, another 1-2 minutes.
  9. Pour the egg mixture evenly over the entire surface of the zucchini and spread with a silicone spatula to seep into every nook and cranny. Be sure to work quickly before the egg begins to set. Let it cook for 1 minute. Carefully flip the whole disk over using 2 long spatulas and cook the other side for 1 more minute.
  10. Slide onto a cutting board and slice like a pizza into 6 pieces. Serve immediately.
